scenes.intention: Show that an AI is given pieces and numbers, not words, and that the count depends on the text, the language and the tokenizer.
scenes.mechanism: One typed message becomes plain text in a card; on the word 'tokenizer' it separates, piece by piece, into chips (a dot marks a leading space). Remind and Jio are outlined where they break. Each chip gains its ID; the chips dim and the list of ids is what the model gets. Word and token counters sit side by side. An English and a Hindi request fill bars to their real token counts; a dashed row of question marks stands for another tokenizer without inventing its output; a paste, tokenizer, count, send strip closes the working diagram before the full-page takeaway.
pip: Pip watches the message, tilts his head at the cut
Pip points at Remind and at Jio as they break
Pip is surprised at the Hindi count
Pip nods at the check step

tokenizer.name: Qwen3-TTS text tokenizer
tokenizer.note: byte-level BPE; ids belong to this tokenizer
